dos.text: Recite the shahada slowly each morning and reflect on the meaning behind each phrase.
Journal one example of Allah’s unity you noticed in creation or your daily routine.
Pair one prayer or dua with an attribute of Allah you are trying to embody.
Teach a friend a short summary of Rububiyyah, Uloohiyyah, or Asma wa Sifaat.
Keep a gentle reminder visible (sticky note, lock screen) that emphasizes Tawheed.

donts.text: Don’t rush through creed statements without letting the heart absorb the message.
Avoid comparing your spiritual timeline to someone else’s and feeling inadequate.
Don’t place cultural customs above the central creed of Islam.
Avoid calling others wrong before you feel confident in the knowledge you share.
Don’t confuse busy activity with genuine remembrance of Allah.

dos.text: Read a few verses slowly with translation and pause to note one lesson.
Listen to a short recitation after reading to connect the meaning with melody.
Record a question or reflection in a journal after each session.
Share a brief reminder from the Quran with a friend or family member.
Seek clarification from a trusted teacher when a verse puzzles you.

donts.text: Avoid racing through pages without savoring the meaning.
Don’t neglect etiquette like clothing, wudu, or a quiet space before reciting.
Don’t rely only on transliteration practice Arabic reading whenever possible.
Avoid ignoring the relevance of the Quran to your daily dilemmas.
Don’t skip back over verses you don’t understand; ask questions instead.

dos.text: Create a short list of his manners and try one new habit each week.
Send salutations every time his name appears in your reading.
Use his mercy stories to guide how you respond to criticism.
Share a small seerah excerpt with someone while highlighting the lesson.
Ask Allah to make you love the Prophet ﷺ more and emulate him sincerely.

donts.text: Don’t reduce his life to legends; stick to authentic narrations.
Avoid criticizing companions without understanding their context.
Don’t admire him only in theory put his kindness into practice.
Don’t treat his guidance as optional when making decisions.
Avoid sharing stories without verifying their authenticity.

dos.text: Note the purpose of each practice before you perform it.
Start with one small practice and build consistency.
Discuss your goals with a mentor to stay accountable.
Pair routines with brief dua so they feel sacred.
Remember service and kindness complete the pillars.

donts.text: Don’t treat rituals as mere chores without heart.
Avoid overloading yourself with every pillar at once.
Don’t skip learning the wisdom behind each pillar.
Avoid comparing your habits to others in a negative way.
Don’t perform practices to impress people rather than Allah.

dos.text: Stand quietly before prayer to settle your mind and intention.
Learn the meaning of each surah you recite.
Add a short dua after every prayer asking for focus.
Pray with a friend or family member to stay motivated.
Listen for the silence between ayahs to keep presence.

donts.text: Don’t let fatigue become a repeated excuse.
Avoid racing through rukus and sujud without feeling humility.
Don’t skip the sunnah prayers that calm your heart.
Avoid checking your phone right before prayer.
Don’t let distraction become the norm; retrain your focus.

dos.text: Plan your fasts with intention to grow empathy.
Schedule nightly reflection or gentle taraweeh.
Serve your neighbors by sharing iftar or snacks.
Give charity early in the day to keep generosity flowing.
Keep a gratitude list that mentions lessons from the fast.

donts.text: Avoid starving yourself without balancing nourishment.
Don’t complain about hunger; use it to remember the needy.
Don’t let social media turn the fast into a show.
Avoid ignoring the spiritual goals while focusing on food.
Don’t sleep through suhoor if you can nourish your intention.

dos.text: Practice greeting everyone with a sincere smile.
Offer patience in difficult conversations and listen fully.
Praise others for small acts of kindness.
Think before you speak to ensure words heal.
Share mercy by helping someone in need without expecting thanks.

donts.text: Don’t gossip or pass judgment without full knowledge.
Avoid letting pride block sincere apologies.
Don’t use anger to intimidate or dominate.
Avoid dismissing small acts of kindness as insignificant.
Don’t become neutral when neighbors need you to speak up.

dos.text: Practice listening fully before responding.
Apologize calmly when you bump into someone emotionally.
Learn common words that build bridges across differences.
Praise teamwork and cooperation in your neighborhood.
Offer dua for conflicts to resolve peacefully.

donts.text: Don’t react impulsively when you feel offended.
Avoid judging people based on age, gender, or background.
Don’t stay silent when someone needs respectful support.
Avoid withdrawing from uncomfortable discussions stay constructive.
Don’t underestimate how calm words can heal tension.

dos.text: Study a short prophetic story each week.
List the lesson each prophet teaches you personally.
Share one story that restores hope in hard times.
Pair their perseverance with your current challenge.
Ask Allah to keep their examples alive in your heart.

donts.text: Don’t idolize one prophet while dismissing the rest.
Avoid treating their stories as fiction instead of guidance.
Don’t ignore the context of their challenges.
Avoid using their examples to shame others.
Don’t compare your struggle to theirs without seeking Allah’s help.

dos.text: Visit or imagine the mosque as a peaceful haven before praying.
Learn one mosque tradition and its spiritual meaning.
Help keep the space clean or donate toward upkeep.
Offer a smile or greeting to someone new in the community.
Use the mosque to practice silence and reflection.

donts.text: Don’t ignore etiquette such as covering your hair or removing shoes.
Avoid treating the mosque solely as a performance stage.
Don’t use the space for unrelated arguments.
Avoid lingering disruptions that interfere with others’ focus.
Don’t forget to include dua for the community while you gather.

dos.text: Check your food choices and thank Allah for halal provision.
Speak honestly in business and personal matters.
Protect your time by saying no gently when needed.
Use media that uplifts your iman.
Explain halal choices to others without pressure.

donts.text: Don’t consume anything that confuses your faith.
Avoid promiscuous or exploitative content.
Don’t hide misconduct to protect reputation.
Avoid excessive pride in wealth or status.
Don’t compromise your values for temporary gain.

dos.text: Affirm each person’s dignity before discussing responsibilities.
Listen to the other gender with curiosity and respect.
Collaborate on projects that need both perspectives.
Pray for mutual honor and compassion in your circles.
Speak up for someone being treated unfairly.

donts.text: Don’t reinforce harmful stereotypes that Islam rejects.
Avoid ignoring the strengths of the opposite gender.
Don’t use gender to justify cruelty.
Avoid dismissing consent or mutual agreement.
Don’t keep silent when you witness harassment.

dos.text: Learn the shahada phrase by heart and understand its layers.
Connect with a mentor or local center for welcoming support.
Begin with simple actos of worship that feel manageable.
Celebrate each milestone with gratitude and dua.
Ask Allah for patience while your surroundings adjust.

donts.text: Don’t rush the journey or compare yourself to others.
Avoid hiding questions out of fear of judgment.
Don’t abandon community when you feel lost.
Avoid isolating yourself from learning opportunities.
Don’t belittle your progress; every step is sacred.

dos.text: Plan a simple Eid dua that invites gratitude and mercy.
Share food or treats with neighbors who may feel lonely.
Learn the qurban story to appreciate sacrifice.
Wear clean modest clothing as a sign of celebration.
Send Eid greetings with sincere dua that includes others.

donts.text: Don’t make Eid about over-the-top spending.
Avoid forgetting the spiritual meaning behind the festivities.
Don’t exclude anyone who might want to celebrate quietly.
Avoid turning Eid into a competition over appearances.
Don’t rush the Eid prayer; be present.

dos.text: Remember the scales by linking actions to their eternal outcomes.
Pray for mercy and consistency every night.
Give charity with the reward of paradise in mind.
Use dua to soften the heart and ask for guidance.
Teach a loved one a hadith about the Hereafter.

donts.text: Don’t postpone repentance thinking you have time.
Avoid living only in dunya without thinking of the akhira.
Don’t disregard warnings about arrogance.
Avoid obsessing over minor sins and ignore major opportunities for good.
Don't assume future Allah will accept negligence without effort.
